primary_external_evidence.source: Linux ld.so manual / glibc dynamic-loader semantics
primary_external_evidence.claim: LD_LIBRARY_PATH participates in dependency resolution before default paths.
Dependencies of loaded shared objects are automatically loaded using dynamic-linker search rules.

r1_hypothesis.hypothesis: Pinning only the SQLite DSO hash/source-id is insufficient for pre-guard code identity if its LD_LIBRARY_PATH directory can contain attacker-controlled DT_NEEDED dependencies.
r1_hypothesis.causal_mechanism: The dynamic linker resolves dependencies before the V5 child guard executes; an unpinned dependency can run a constructor while the pinned SQLite-like DSO bytes and functional behavior remain unchanged.
r1_hypothesis.predicted_if_right: A byte-identical pinned DSO can coexist with pre-main constructor execution when only a dependency in the loader search directory changes.
r1_hypothesis.predicted_if_counterhypothesis_right: Changing an unpinned dependency while preserving the pinned DSO hash cannot produce code execution before program logic.

r3_counter_reality.counterhypothesis: The V5 DSO hash/source-id/anchor is sufficient because any meaningful code substitution would necessarily change the pinned SQLite object itself.
r3_counter_reality.falsifier: Hold the pinned DSO bytes and output constant; change only a dependency in the loader search directory and observe whether constructor code runs before program logic.

unusual_experiment.scope_limit: Synthetic ELF dependency topology proves the loader mechanism; it does not by itself prove a malicious dependency exists in the productive Frank SQLite artifact tree.
